## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-gapply--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
# Computes the arithmetic mean of the second column by grouping
# on the first and third columns. Output the grouping values and the average.

df <- createDataFrame (
list(list(1L, 1, "1", 0.1), list(1L, 2, "1", 0.2), list(3L, 3, "3", 0.3)),
  c("a", "b", "c", "d"))

# Here our output contains three columns, the key which is a combination of two
# columns with data types integer and string and the mean which is a double.
schema <- structType(structField("a", "integer"), structField("c", "string"),
  structField("avg", "double"))
result <- gapply(
  df,
  c("a", "c"),
  function(key, x) {
    # key will either be list(1L, '1') (for the group where a=1L,c='1') or
    #   list(3L, '3') (for the group where a=3L,c='3')
    y <- data.frame(key, mean(x$b), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}, schema)

# The schema also can be specified in a DDL-formatted string.
schema <- "a INT, c STRING, avg DOUBLE"
result <- gapply(
  df,
  c("a", "c"),
  function(key, x) {
    y <- data.frame(key, mean(x$b), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}, schema)

# We can also group the data and afterwards call gapply on GroupedData.
# For example:
gdf <- group_by(df, "a", "c")
result <- gapply(
  gdf,
  function(key, x) {
    y <- data.frame(key, mean(x$b), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}, schema)
collect(result)

# Result
# ------
# a c avg
# 3 3 3.0
# 1 1 1.5

# Fits linear models on iris dataset by grouping on the 'Species' column and
# using 'Sepal_Length' as a target variable, 'Sepal_Width', 'Petal_Length'
# and 'Petal_Width' as training features.

df <- createDataFrame (iris)
schema <- structType(structField("(Intercept)", "double"),
  structField("Sepal_Width", "double"),structField("Petal_Length", "double"),
  structField("Petal_Width", "double"))
df1 <- gapply(
  df,
  df$"Species",
  function(key, x) {
    m <- suppressWarnings(lm(Sepal_Length ~
    Sepal_Width + Petal_Length + Petal_Width, x))
    data.frame(t(coef(m)))
  }, schema)
collect(df1)

# Result
# ---------
# Model  (Intercept)  Sepal_Width  Petal_Length  Petal_Width
# 1        0.699883    0.3303370    0.9455356    -0.1697527
# 2        1.895540    0.3868576    0.9083370    -0.6792238
# 3        2.351890    0.6548350    0.2375602     0.2521257

}
```

# gapplyCollect

`gapplyCollect.Rd`

Groups the SparkDataFrame using the specified columns, applies the R function to each
group and collects the result back to R as data.frame.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-gapplycollect--ref-usage)

```text
gapplyCollect(x, ...)

# S4 method for GroupedData
gapplyCollect(x, func)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
gapplyCollect(x, cols, func)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-gapplycollect--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame or GroupedData.
- ...

  additional argument(s) passed to the method.
- func

  a function to be applied to each group partition specified by grouping
  column of the SparkDataFrame. See Details.
- cols

  grouping columns.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-gapplycollect--value)

A data.frame.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-gapplycollect--details)

`func` is a function of two arguments. The first, usually named `key`
(though this is not enforced) corresponds to the grouping key, will be an
unnamed `list` of `length(cols)` length-one objects corresponding
to the grouping columns' values for the current group.

The second, herein `x`, will be a local `[data.frame](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html)` with the
columns of the input not in `cols` for the rows corresponding to `key`.

The output of `func` must be a `data.frame` matching `schema` --
in particular this means the names of the output `data.frame` are irrelevant

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-gapplycollect--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
# Computes the arithmetic mean of the second column by grouping
# on the first and third columns. Output the grouping values and the average.

df <- createDataFrame (
list(list(1L, 1, "1", 0.1), list(1L, 2, "1", 0.2), list(3L, 3, "3", 0.3)),
  c("a", "b", "c", "d"))

result <- gapplyCollect(
  df,
  c("a", "c"),
  function(key, x) {
    y <- data.frame(key, mean(x$b), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(y) <- c("key_a", "key_c", "mean_b")
    y
  })

# We can also group the data and afterwards call gapply on GroupedData.
# For example:
gdf <- group_by(df, "a", "c")
result <- gapplyCollect(
  gdf,
  function(key, x) {
    y <- data.frame(key, mean(x$b), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(y) <- c("key_a", "key_c", "mean_b")
    y
  })

# Result
# ------
# key_a key_c mean_b
# 3 3 3.0
# 1 1 1.5

# Fits linear models on iris dataset by grouping on the 'Species' column and
# using 'Sepal_Length' as a target variable, 'Sepal_Width', 'Petal_Length'
# and 'Petal_Width' as training features.

df <- createDataFrame (iris)
result <- gapplyCollect(
  df,
  df$"Species",
  function(key, x) {
    m <- suppressWarnings(lm(Sepal_Length ~
    Sepal_Width + Petal_Length + Petal_Width, x))
    data.frame(t(coef(m)))
  })

# Result
# ---------
# Model  X.Intercept.  Sepal_Width  Petal_Length  Petal_Width
# 1        0.699883    0.3303370    0.9455356    -0.1697527
# 2        1.895540    0.3868576    0.9083370    -0.6792238
# 3        2.351890    0.6548350    0.2375602     0.2521257

}
```

```text
if (FALSE) {
  # Compute the average for all numeric columns grouped by department.
  avg(groupBy(df, "department"))

  # Compute the max age and average salary, grouped by department and gender.
  agg(groupBy(df, "department", "gender"), salary="avg", "age" -> "max")
}
```

# Head

`head.Rd`

Return the first `num` rows of a SparkDataFrame as a R data.frame. If `num` is not
specified, then head() returns the first 6 rows as with R data.frame.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-head--ref-usage)

```bash
# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
head(x, num = 6L)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-head--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- num

  the number of rows to return. Default is 6.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-head--value)

A data.frame.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-head--note)

head since 1.4.0

# Compute histogram statistics for given column

`histogram.Rd`

This function computes a histogram for a given SparkR Column.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-histogram--ref-usage)

```bash
# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,characterOrColumn
histogram(df, col, nbins = 10)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-histogram--arguments)

- df

  the SparkDataFrame containing the Column to build the histogram from.
- col

  the column as Character string or a Column to build the histogram from.
- nbins

  the number of bins (optional). Default value is 10.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-histogram--value)

a data.frame with the histogram statistics, i.e., counts and centroids.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-histogram--note)

histogram since 2.0.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-histogram--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {

# Create a SparkDataFrame from the Iris dataset
irisDF <- createDataFrame(iris)

# Compute histogram statistics
histStats <- histogram(irisDF, irisDF$Sepal_Length, nbins = 12)

# Once SparkR has computed the histogram statistics, the histogram can be
# rendered using the ggplot2 library:

require(ggplot2)
plot <- ggplot(histStats, aes(x = centroids, y = counts)) +
        geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
        xlab("Sepal_Length") + ylab("Frequency")
}
```

# insertInto

`insertInto.Rd`

Insert the contents of a SparkDataFrame into a table registered in the current SparkSession.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-insertinto--ref-usage)

```sql
insertInto(x, tableName, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,character
insertInto(x, tableName, overwrite = FALSE)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-insertinto--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- tableName

  a character vector containing the name of the table.
- ...

  further arguments to be passed to or from other methods.
  the existing rows in the table.
- overwrite

  a logical argument indicating whether or not to overwrite.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-insertinto--note)

insertInto since 1.4.0

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Download and Install Apache Spark to a Local Directory

`install.spark.Rd`

`install.spark` downloads and installs Spark to a local directory if
it is not found. If SPARK\_HOME is set in the environment, and that directory is found, that is
returned. The Spark version we use is the same as the SparkR version. Users can specify a desired
Hadoop version, the remote mirror site, and the directory where the package is installed locally.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--ref-usage)

```text
install.spark(
  hadoopVersion = "3",
  mirrorUrl = NULL,
  localDir = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--arguments)

- hadoopVersion

  Version of Hadoop to install. Default is `"3"`.
  If `hadoopVersion = "without"`, "Hadoop free" build is installed.
  See
  [
  "Hadoop Free" Build](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-hadoop-provided) for more information.
  Other patched version names can also be used.
- mirrorUrl

  base URL of the repositories to use. The directory layout should follow
  [Apache mirrors](https://www.apache.org/dyn/closer.lua/spark/).
- localDir

  a local directory where Spark is installed. The directory contains
  version-specific folders of Spark packages. Default is path to
  the cache directory:

  - Mac OS X: `~/Library/Caches/spark`
  - Unix: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` if defined, otherwise `~/.cache/spark`
  - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Apache\Spark\Cache`.
- overwrite

  If `TRUE`, download and overwrite the existing tar file in localDir
  and force re-install Spark (in case the local directory or file is corrupted)

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--value)

the (invisible) local directory where Spark is found or installed

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--details)

The full url of remote file is inferred from `mirrorUrl` and `hadoopVersion`.
`mirrorUrl` specifies the remote path to a Spark folder. It is followed by a subfolder
named after the Spark version (that corresponds to SparkR), and then the tar filename.
The filename is composed of four parts, i.e. [Spark version]-bin-[Hadoop version].tgz.
For example, the full path for a Spark 3.3.1 package from
`https://archive.apache.org` has path:
`http://archive.apache.org/dist/spark/spark-3.3.1/spark-3.3.1-bin-hadoop3.tgz`.
For `hadoopVersion = "without"`, [Hadoop version] in the filename is then
`without-hadoop`.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--note)

install.spark since 2.1.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--see-also)

See available Hadoop versions:
[Apache Spark](https://spark.apache.org/downloads.html)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-install-spark--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
install.spark()
}
```

# intersectAll

`intersectAll.Rd`

Return a new SparkDataFrame containing rows in both this SparkDataFrame
and another SparkDataFrame while preserving the duplicates.
This is equivalent to `INTERSECT ALL` in SQL. Also as standard in
SQL, this function resolves columns by position (not by name).

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-intersectall--ref-usage)

```text
intersectAll(x, y)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,SparkDataFrame
intersectAll(x, y)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-intersectall--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- y

  a SparkDataFrame.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-intersectall--value)

A SparkDataFrame containing the result of the intersect all operation.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-intersectall--note)

intersectAll since 2.4.0

# isStreaming

`isStreaming.Rd`

Returns TRUE if this SparkDataFrame contains one or more sources that continuously return data
as it arrives. A dataset that reads data from a streaming source must be executed as a
`StreamingQuery` using `write.stream`.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-isstreaming--ref-usage)

```text
isStreaming(x)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
isStreaming(x)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-isstreaming--arguments)

- x

  A SparkDataFrame

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-isstreaming--value)

TRUE if this SparkDataFrame is from a streaming source

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-isstreaming--note)

isStreaming since 2.2.0

experimental

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-isstreaming--see-also)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Join

`join.Rd`

Joins two SparkDataFrames based on the given join expression.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--ref-usage)

```bash
# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,SparkDataFrame
join(x, y, joinExpr = NULL, joinType = NULL)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--arguments)

- x

  A SparkDataFrame
- y

  A SparkDataFrame
- joinExpr

  (Optional) The expression used to perform the join. joinExpr must be a
  Column expression. If joinExpr is omitted, the default, inner join is attempted and an error is
  thrown if it would be a Cartesian Product. For Cartesian join, use crossJoin instead.
- joinType

  The type of join to perform, default 'inner'.
  Must be one of: 'inner', 'cross', 'outer', 'full', 'fullouter', 'full\_outer',
  'left', 'leftouter', 'left\_outer', 'right', 'rightouter', 'right\_outer', 'semi',
  'leftsemi', 'left\_semi', 'anti', 'leftanti', 'left\_anti'.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--value)

A SparkDataFrame containing the result of the join operation.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--note)

join since 1.4.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--see-also)

[merge](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-merge) [crossJoin](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-crossjoin)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-join--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
df1 <- read.json(path)
df2 <- read.json(path2)
join(df1, df2, df1$col1 == df2$col2) # Performs an inner join based on expression
join(df1, df2, df1$col1 == df2$col2, "right_outer")
join(df1, df2) # Attempts an inner join
}
```

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# last

`last.Rd`

Aggregate function: returns the last value in a group.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--ref-usage)

```text
last(x, ...)

# S4 method for characterOrColumn
last(x, na.rm = FALSE)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--arguments)

- x

  column to compute on.
- ...

  further arguments to be passed to or from other methods.
- na.rm

  a logical value indicating whether NA values should be stripped
  before the computation proceeds.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--details)

The function by default returns the last values it sees. It will return the last non-missing
value it sees when na.rm is set to true. If all values are missing, then NA is returned.
Note: the function is non-deterministic because its results depends on the order of the rows
which may be non-deterministic after a shuffle.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--note)

last since 1.4.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--see-also)

Other aggregate functions:
`[avg](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-avg)()`,
`[column_aggregate_functions](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-column_aggregate_functions)`,
`[corr](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-corr)()`,
`[count](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-count)()`,
`[cov](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-cov)()`,
`[first](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-first)()`

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-last--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
last(df$c)
last(df$c, TRUE)
}
```

```text
listColumns(tableName, databaseName = NULL)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-listcolumns--arguments)

- tableName

  the qualified or unqualified name that designates a table/view. If no database
  identifier is provided, it refers to a table/view in the current database.
  If `databaseName` parameter is specified, this must be an unqualified name.
  The table name can be qualified with catalog name since 3.4.0, when databaseName
  is NULL.

# localCheckpoint

`localCheckpoint.Rd`

Returns a locally checkpointed version of this SparkDataFrame. Checkpointing can be used to
truncate the logical plan, which is especially useful in iterative algorithms where the plan
may grow exponentially. Local checkpoints are stored in the executors using the caching
subsystem and therefore they are not reliable.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-localcheckpoint--ref-usage)

```text
localCheckpoint(x, eager = TRUE)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
localCheckpoint(x, eager = TRUE)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-localcheckpoint--arguments)

- x

  A SparkDataFrame
- eager

  whether to locally checkpoint this SparkDataFrame immediately

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-localcheckpoint--value)

a new locally checkpointed SparkDataFrame

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-localcheckpoint--note)

localCheckpoint since 2.3.0

# Match a column with given values.

`match.Rd`

Match a column with given values.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-match--ref-usage)

```bash
# S4 method for Column
%in%(x, table)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-match--arguments)

- x

  a Column.
- table

  a collection of values (coercible to list) to compare with.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-match--value)

A matched values as a result of comparing with given values.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-match--note)

%in% since 1.5.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-match--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
filter(df, "age in (10, 30)")
where(df, df$age %in% c(10, 30))
}
```

![]()

# Merges two data frames

`merge.Rd`

Merges two data frames

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-merge--ref-usage)

```text
merge(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,SparkDataFrame
merge(
  x,
  y,
  by = intersect(names(x), names(y)),
  by.x = by,
  by.y = by,
  all = FALSE,
  all.x = all,
  all.y = all,
  sort = TRUE,
  suffixes = c("_x", "_y"),
  ...
)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-merge--arguments)

- x

  the first data frame to be joined.
- y

  the second data frame to be joined.
- ...

  additional argument(s) passed to the method.
- by

  a character vector specifying the join columns. If by is not
  specified, the common column names in `x` and `y` will be used.
  If by or both by.x and by.y are explicitly set to NULL or of length 0, the Cartesian
  Product of x and y will be returned.
- by.x

  a character vector specifying the joining columns for x.
- by.y

  a character vector specifying the joining columns for y.
- all

  a boolean value setting `all.x` and `all.y`
  if any of them are unset.
- all.x

  a boolean value indicating whether all the rows in x should
  be including in the join.
- all.y

  a boolean value indicating whether all the rows in y should
  be including in the join.
- sort

  a logical argument indicating whether the resulting columns should be sorted.
- suffixes

  a string vector of length 2 used to make colnames of
  `x` and `y` unique.
  The first element is appended to each colname of `x`.
  The second element is appended to each colname of `y`.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-merge--details)

If all.x and all.y are set to FALSE, a natural join will be returned. If
all.x is set to TRUE and all.y is set to FALSE, a left outer join will
be returned. If all.x is set to FALSE and all.y is set to TRUE, a right
outer join will be returned. If all.x and all.y are set to TRUE, a full
outer join will be returned.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-merge--note)

merge since 1.5.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-merge--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
df1 <- read.json(path)
df2 <- read.json(path2)
merge(df1, df2) # Performs an inner join by common columns
merge(df1, df2, by = "col1") # Performs an inner join based on expression
merge(df1, df2, by.x = "col1", by.y = "col2", all.y = TRUE)
merge(df1, df2, by.x = "col1", by.y = "col2", all.x = TRUE)
merge(df1, df2, by.x = "col1", by.y = "col2", all.x = TRUE, all.y = TRUE)
merge(df1, df2, by.x = "col1", by.y = "col2", all = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
merge(df1, df2, by = "col1", all = TRUE, suffixes = c("-X", "-Y"))
merge(df1, df2, by = NULL) # Performs a Cartesian join
}
```

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
path <- "path/to/file.json"
df <- read.json(path)
newDF <- mutate(df, newCol = df$col1 * 5, newCol2 = df$col1 * 2)
names(newDF) # Will contain newCol, newCol2
newDF2 <- transform(df, newCol = df$col1 / 5, newCol2 = df$col1 * 2)

df <- createDataFrame(list(list("Andy", 30L), list("Justin", 19L)), c("name", "age"))
# Replace the "age" column
df1 <- mutate(df, age = df$age + 1L)
}
```

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-nafunctions--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# A set of SparkDataFrame functions working with NA values

`nafunctions.Rd`

dropna, na.omit - Returns a new SparkDataFrame omitting rows with null values.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-nafunctions--ref-usage)

```text
dropna(x, how = c("any", "all"), minNonNulls = NULL, cols = NULL)

na.omit(object, ...)

fillna(x, value, cols = NULL)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
dropna(x, how = c("any", "all"), minNonNulls = NULL, cols = NULL)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
na.omit(object, how = c("any", "all"), minNonNulls = NULL, cols = NULL)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
fillna(x, value, cols = NULL)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-nafunctions--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- how

  "any" or "all".
  if "any", drop a row if it contains any nulls.
  if "all", drop a row only if all its values are null.
  if `minNonNulls` is specified, how is ignored.
- minNonNulls

  if specified, drop rows that have less than
  `minNonNulls` non-null values.
  This overwrites the how parameter.
- cols

  optional list of column names to consider. In `fillna`,
  columns specified in cols that do not have matching data
  type are ignored. For example, if value is a character, and
  subset contains a non-character column, then the non-character
  column is simply ignored.
- object

  a SparkDataFrame.
- ...

  further arguments to be passed to or from other methods.
- value

  value to replace null values with.
  Should be an integer, numeric, character or named list.
  If the value is a named list, then cols is ignored and
  value must be a mapping from column name (character) to
  replacement value. The replacement value must be an
  integer, numeric or character.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-nafunctions--value)

A SparkDataFrame.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-nafunctions--note)

dropna since 1.4.0

na.omit since 1.5.0

fillna since 1.4.0

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# !

`not.Rd`

Inversion of boolean expression.

Inversion of boolean expression.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--ref-usage)

```text
not(x)

# S4 method for Column
!(x)

# S4 method for Column
not(x)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--arguments)

- x

  Column to compute on

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--details)

`not` and `!` cannot be applied directly to numerical column.
To achieve R-like truthiness column has to be casted to `BooleanType`.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--note)

! since 2.3.0

not since 2.3.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--see-also)

Other non-aggregate functions:
`[column_nonaggregate_functions](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-column_nonaggregate_functions)`,
`[column](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-column)()`

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-not--ref-examples)

```sql
if (FALSE) {
df <- createDataFrame(data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1)))

head(select(df, !column("x") > 0))
}
if (FALSE) {
df <- createDataFrame(data.frame(
  is_true = c(TRUE, FALSE, NA),
  flag = c(1, 0,  1)
))

head(select(df, not(df$is_true)))

# Explicit cast is required when working with numeric column
head(select(df, not(cast(df$flag, "boolean"))))
}
```

[Skip to contents](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--main)

[
![](https://spark.apache.org/images/spark-logo-rev.svg)](https://spark.apache.org/)
[SparkR](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-index)
4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# over

`over.Rd`

Define a windowing column.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--ref-usage)

```text
over(x, window)

# S4 method for Column,WindowSpec
over(x, window)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--arguments)

- x

  a Column, usually one returned by window function(s).
- window

  a WindowSpec object. Can be created by `windowPartitionBy` or
  `windowOrderBy` and configured by other WindowSpec methods.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--note)

over since 2.0.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--see-also)

Other column\_func:
`[alias](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-alias)()`,
`[between](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-between)()`,
`[cast](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-cast)()`,
`[endsWith](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-endswith)()`,
`[otherwise](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-otherwise)()`,
`[startsWith](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-startswith)()`,
`[substr](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-substr)()`

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-over--ref-examples)

```sql
if (FALSE) {
  df <- createDataFrame(mtcars)

  # Partition by am (transmission) and order by hp (horsepower)
  ws <- orderBy(windowPartitionBy("am"), "hp")

  # Rank on hp within each partition
  out <- select(df, over(rank(), ws), df$hp, df$am)

  # Lag mpg values by 1 row on the partition-and-ordered table
  out <- select(df, over(lead(df$mpg), ws), df$mpg, df$hp, df$am)
}
```

```text
  partitionBy(ws, "col1", "col2")
```

# Persist

`persist.Rd`

Persist this SparkDataFrame with the specified storage level. For details of the
supported storage levels, refer to
[https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/rdd-programming-guide.html#rdd-persistence](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-rdd-programming-guide--rdd-persistence).

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-persist--ref-usage)

```text
persist(x, newLevel)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,character
persist(x, newLevel)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-persist--arguments)

- x

  the SparkDataFrame to persist.
- newLevel

  storage level chosen for the persistence. See available options in
  the description.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-persist--note)

persist since 1.4.0

# Pivot a column of the GroupedData and perform the specified aggregation. — pivot • SparkR

[Skip to contents](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--main)

[
![](https://spark.apache.org/images/spark-logo-rev.svg)](https://spark.apache.org/)
[SparkR](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-index)
4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Pivot a column of the GroupedData and perform the specified aggregation.

`pivot.Rd`

Pivot a column of the GroupedData and perform the specified aggregation.
There are two versions of pivot function: one that requires the caller to specify the list
of distinct values to pivot on, and one that does not. The latter is more concise but less
efficient, because Spark needs to first compute the list of distinct values internally.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--ref-usage)

```bash
# S4 method for GroupedData,character
pivot(x, colname, values = list())
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--arguments)

- x

  a GroupedData object
- colname

  A column name
- values

  A value or a list/vector of distinct values for the output columns.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--value)

GroupedData object

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--note)

pivot since 2.0.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-pivot--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
df <- createDataFrame(data.frame(
    earnings = c(10000, 10000, 11000, 15000, 12000, 20000, 21000, 22000),
    course = c("R", "Python", "R", "Python", "R", "Python", "R", "Python"),
    period = c("1H", "1H", "2H", "2H", "1H", "1H", "2H", "2H"),
    year = c(2015, 2015, 2015, 2015, 2016, 2016, 2016, 2016)
))
group_sum <- sum(pivot(groupBy(df, "year"), "course"), "earnings")
group_min <- min(pivot(groupBy(df, "year"), "course", "R"), "earnings")
group_max <- max(pivot(groupBy(df, "year"), "course", c("Python", "R")), "earnings")
group_mean <- mean(pivot(groupBy(df, "year"), "course", list("Python", "R")), "earnings")
}
```

# randomSplit

`randomSplit.Rd`

Return a list of randomly split dataframes with the provided weights.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-randomsplit--ref-usage)

```text
randomSplit(x, weights, seed)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,numeric
randomSplit(x, weights, seed)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-randomsplit--arguments)

- x

  A SparkDataFrame
- weights

  A vector of weights for splits, will be normalized if they don't sum to 1
- seed

  A seed to use for random split

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-randomsplit--note)

randomSplit since 2.0.0

4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# rangeBetween

`rangeBetween.Rd`

Defines the frame boundaries, from `start` (inclusive) to `end` (inclusive).

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--ref-usage)

```text
rangeBetween(x, start, end)

# S4 method for WindowSpec,numeric,numeric
rangeBetween(x, start, end)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--arguments)

- x

  a WindowSpec
- start

  boundary start, inclusive.
  The frame is unbounded if this is the minimum long value.
- end

  boundary end, inclusive.
  The frame is unbounded if this is the maximum long value.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--value)

a WindowSpec

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--details)

Both `start` and `end` are relative from the current row. For example, "0" means
"current row", while "-1" means one off before the current row, and "5" means the five off
after the current row.

We recommend users use `Window.unboundedPreceding`, `Window.unboundedFollowing`,
and `Window.currentRow` to specify special boundary values, rather than using long values
directly.

A range-based boundary is based on the actual value of the ORDER BY
expression(s). An offset is used to alter the value of the ORDER BY expression,
for instance if the current ORDER BY expression has a value of 10 and the lower bound offset
is -3, the resulting lower bound for the current row will be 10 - 3 = 7. This however puts a
number of constraints on the ORDER BY expressions: there can be only one expression and this
expression must have a numerical data type. An exception can be made when the offset is
unbounded, because no value modification is needed, in this case multiple and non-numeric
ORDER BY expression are allowed.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--note)

rangeBetween since 2.0.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--see-also)

Other windowspec\_method:
`[orderBy](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-orderby)()`,
`[partitionBy](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-partitionby)()`,
`[rowsBetween](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween)()`

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
  id <- c(rep(1, 3), rep(2, 3), 3)
  desc <- c('New', 'New', 'Good', 'New', 'Good', 'Good', 'New')
  df <- data.frame(id, desc)
  df <- createDataFrame(df)
  w1 <- orderBy(windowPartitionBy('desc'), df$id)
  w2 <- rangeBetween(w1, 0, 3)
  df1 <- withColumn(df, "sum", over(sum(df$id), w2))
  head(df1)
}
```

# Union two or more SparkDataFrames

`rbind.Rd`

Union two or more SparkDataFrames by row. As in R's `rbind`, this method
requires that the input SparkDataFrames have the same column names.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rbind--ref-usage)

```text
rbind(..., deparse.level = 1)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
rbind(x, ..., deparse.level = 1)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rbind--arguments)

- ...

  additional SparkDataFrame(s).
- deparse.level

  currently not used (put here to match the signature of
  the base implementation).
- x

  a SparkDataFrame.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rbind--value)

A SparkDataFrame containing the result of the union.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rbind--details)

Note: This does not remove duplicate rows across the two SparkDataFrames.

# Create a SparkDataFrame representing the database table accessible via JDBC URL — read.jdbc • SparkR

[Skip to contents](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--main)

[
![](https://spark.apache.org/images/spark-logo-rev.svg)](https://spark.apache.org/)
[SparkR](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-index)
4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Create a SparkDataFrame representing the database table accessible via JDBC URL

`read.jdbc.Rd`

Additional JDBC database connection properties can be set (...)
You can find the JDBC-specific option and parameter documentation for reading tables via JDBC in
[https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-data-sources-jdbc.html#data-source-option](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-sql-data-sources-jdbc--data-source-option)Data Source Option in the version you use.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--ref-usage)

```text
read.jdbc(
  url,
  tableName,
  partitionColumn = NULL,
  lowerBound = NULL,
  upperBound = NULL,
  numPartitions = 0L,
  predicates = list(),
  ...
)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--arguments)

- url

  JDBC database url of the form `jdbc:subprotocol:subname`
- tableName

  the name of the table in the external database
- partitionColumn

  the name of a column of numeric, date, or timestamp type
  that will be used for partitioning.
- lowerBound

  the minimum value of `partitionColumn` used to decide partition stride
- upperBound

  the maximum value of `partitionColumn` used to decide partition stride
- numPartitions

  the number of partitions, This, along with `lowerBound` (inclusive),
  `upperBound` (exclusive), form partition strides for generated WHERE
  clause expressions used to split the column `partitionColumn` evenly.
  This defaults to SparkContext.defaultParallelism when unset.
- predicates

  a list of conditions in the where clause; each one defines one partition
- ...

  additional JDBC database connection named properties.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--value)

SparkDataFrame

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--details)

Only one of partitionColumn or predicates should be set. Partitions of the table will be
retrieved in parallel based on the `numPartitions` or by the predicates.

Don't create too many partitions in parallel on a large cluster; otherwise Spark might crash
your external database systems.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--note)

read.jdbc since 2.0.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-jdbc--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
jdbcUrl <- "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/databasename"
df <- read.jdbc(jdbcUrl, "table", predicates = list("field<=123"), user = "username")
df2 <- read.jdbc(jdbcUrl, "table2", partitionColumn = "index", lowerBound = 0,
                 upperBound = 10000, user = "username", password = "password")
}
```

# Create a SparkDataFrame from a JSON file.

`read.json.Rd`

Loads a JSON file, returning the result as a SparkDataFrame
By default, ([JSON Lines text format or newline-delimited JSON](https://jsonlines.org/)
) is supported. For JSON (one record per file), set a named property `multiLine` to
`TRUE`.
It goes through the entire dataset once to determine the schema.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-json--ref-usage)

```text
read.json(path, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-json--arguments)

- path

  Path of file to read. A vector of multiple paths is allowed.
- ...

  additional external data source specific named properties.
  You can find the JSON-specific options for reading JSON files in
  [https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-data-sources-json.html#data-source-option](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-sql-data-sources-json--data-source-option)Data Source Option in the version you use.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-json--value)

SparkDataFrame

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-json--note)

read.json since 1.6.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-json--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
path <- "path/to/file.json"
df <- read.json(path)
df <- read.json(path, multiLine = TRUE)
}
```

4.1.1

- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Load a streaming SparkDataFrame

`read.stream.Rd`

Returns the dataset in a data source as a SparkDataFrame

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--ref-usage)

```text
read.stream(source = NULL, schema = NULL, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--arguments)

- source

  The name of external data source
- schema

  The data schema defined in structType or a DDL-formatted string, this is
  required for file-based streaming data source
- ...

  additional external data source specific named options, for instance `path` for
  file-based streaming data source. `timeZone` to indicate a timezone to be used to
  parse timestamps in the JSON/CSV data sources or partition values; If it isn't set, it
  uses the default value, session local timezone.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--value)

SparkDataFrame

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--details)

The data source is specified by the `source` and a set of options(...).
If `source` is not specified, the default data source configured by
"spark.sql.sources.default" will be used.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--note)

read.stream since 2.2.0

experimental

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--see-also)

[write.stream](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-write-stream)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-stream--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
df <- read.stream("socket", host = "localhost", port = 9999)
q <- write.stream(df, "text", path = "/home/user/out", checkpointLocation = "/home/user/cp")

df <- read.stream("json", path = jsonDir, schema = schema, maxFilesPerTrigger = 1)
stringSchema <- "name STRING, info MAP<STRING, DOUBLE>"
df1 <- read.stream("json", path = jsonDir, schema = stringSchema, maxFilesPerTrigger = 1)
}
```

# Create a SparkDataFrame from a text file.

a string column named "value", and followed by partitioned columns if
there are any. The text files must be encoded as UTF-8.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-text--ref-usage)

```text
read.text(path, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-text--arguments)

- path

  Path of file to read. A vector of multiple paths is allowed.
- ...

  additional external data source specific named properties.
  You can find the text-specific options for reading text files in
  [https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-data-sources-text.html#data-source-option](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-sql-data-sources-text--data-source-option)Data Source Option in the version you use.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-text--value)

SparkDataFrame

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-text--details)

Each line in the text file is a new row in the resulting SparkDataFrame.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-text--note)

read.text since 1.6.1

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-text--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
path <- "path/to/file.txt"
df <- read.text(path)
}
```

![]()

# Invalidates and refreshes all the cached data and metadata of the given table

`refreshTable.Rd`

Invalidates and refreshes all the cached data and metadata of the given table. For performance
reasons, Spark SQL or the external data source library it uses might cache certain metadata about
a table, such as the location of blocks. When those change outside of Spark SQL, users should
call this function to invalidate the cache.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-refreshtable--ref-usage)

```text
refreshTable(tableName)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-refreshtable--arguments)

- tableName

  the qualified or unqualified name that designates a table. If no database
  identifier is provided, it refers to a table in the current database.
  The table name can be fully qualified with catalog name since 3.4.0.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-refreshtable--details)

If this table is cached as an InMemoryRelation, drop the original cached version and make the
new version cached lazily.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-refreshtable--note)

since 2.2.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-refreshtable--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
refreshTable("spark_catalog.default.myTable")
}
```

- existingCol

  The name of the column you want to change.
- newCol

  The new column name.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rename--value)

A SparkDataFrame with the column name changed.

withColumnRenamed since 1.4.0

rename since 1.4.0

# Repartition

`repartition.Rd`

The following options for repartition are possible:

- 1. Return a new SparkDataFrame that has exactly `numPartitions`.
- 2. Return a new SparkDataFrame hash partitioned by
  the given columns into `numPartitions`.
- 3. Return a new SparkDataFrame hash partitioned by the given column(s),
  using `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` as number of partitions.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartition--ref-usage)

```text
repartition(x, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
repartition(x, numPartitions = NULL, col = NULL, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartition--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- ...

  additional column(s) to be used in the partitioning.
- numPartitions

  the number of partitions to use.
- col

  the column by which the partitioning will be performed.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartition--note)

repartition since 1.4.0

![]()

# Repartition by range

`repartitionByRange.Rd`

The following options for repartition by range are possible:

- 1. Return a new SparkDataFrame range partitioned by
  the given columns into `numPartitions`.
- 2. Return a new SparkDataFrame range partitioned by the given column(s),
  using `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` as number of partitions.

At least one partition-by expression must be specified.
When no explicit sort order is specified, "ascending nulls first" is assumed.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartitionbyrange--ref-usage)

```text
repartitionByRange(x, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
repartitionByRange(x, numPartitions = NULL, col = NULL, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartitionbyrange--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- ...

  additional column(s) to be used in the range partitioning.
- numPartitions

  the number of partitions to use.
- col

  the column by which the range partitioning will be performed.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartitionbyrange--details)

Note that due to performance reasons this method uses sampling to estimate the ranges.
Hence, the output may not be consistent, since sampling can return different values.
The sample size can be controlled by the config
`spark.sql.execution.rangeExchange.sampleSizePerPartition`.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartitionbyrange--note)

repartitionByRange since 2.4.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-repartitionbyrange--see-also)

# rollup

`rollup.Rd`

Create a multi-dimensional rollup for the SparkDataFrame using the specified columns.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rollup--ref-usage)

```text
rollup(x, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
rollup(x, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rollup--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- ...

  character name(s) or Column(s) to group on.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rollup--value)

A GroupedData.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rollup--details)

If grouping expression is missing `rollup` creates a single global aggregate and is
equivalent to direct application of [agg](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-summarize).

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rollup--note)

rollup since 2.3.0

```text
}
```

# rowsBetween — rowsBetween • SparkR

4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# rowsBetween

`rowsBetween.Rd`

Defines the frame boundaries, from `start` (inclusive) to `end` (inclusive).

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--ref-usage)

```text
rowsBetween(x, start, end)

# S4 method for WindowSpec,numeric,numeric
rowsBetween(x, start, end)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--arguments)

- x

  a WindowSpec
- start

  boundary start, inclusive.
  The frame is unbounded if this is the minimum long value.
- end

  boundary end, inclusive.
  The frame is unbounded if this is the maximum long value.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--value)

a WindowSpec

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--details)

Both `start` and `end` are relative positions from the current row. For example,
"0" means "current row", while "-1" means the row before the current row, and "5" means the
fifth row after the current row.

We recommend users use `Window.unboundedPreceding`, `Window.unboundedFollowing`,
and `Window.currentRow` to specify special boundary values, rather than using long values
directly.

A row based boundary is based on the position of the row within the partition.
An offset indicates the number of rows above or below the current row, the frame for the
current row starts or ends. For instance, given a row based sliding frame with a lower bound
offset of -1 and a upper bound offset of +2. The frame for row with index 5 would range from
index 4 to index 7.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--note)

rowsBetween since 2.0.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--see-also)

Other windowspec\_method:
`[orderBy](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-orderby)()`,
`[partitionBy](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-partitionby)()`,
`[rangeBetween](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rangebetween)()`

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-rowsbetween--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
  id <- c(rep(1, 3), rep(2, 3), 3)
  desc <- c('New', 'New', 'Good', 'New', 'Good', 'Good', 'New')
  df <- data.frame(id, desc)
  df <- createDataFrame(df)
  w1 <- orderBy(windowPartitionBy('desc'), df$id)
  w2 <- rowsBetween(w1, 0, 3)
  df1 <- withColumn(df, "sum", over(sum(df$id), w2))
  head(df1)
}
```

# Sample

`sample.Rd`

Return a sampled subset of this SparkDataFrame using a random seed.
Note: this is not guaranteed to provide exactly the fraction specified
of the total count of of the given SparkDataFrame.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sample--ref-usage)

```text
sample(x, withReplacement = FALSE, fraction, seed)

sample_frac(x, withReplacement = FALSE, fraction, seed)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
sample(x, withReplacement = FALSE, fraction, seed)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
sample_frac(x, withReplacement = FALSE, fraction, seed)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sample--arguments)

- x

  A SparkDataFrame
- withReplacement

  Sampling with replacement or not
- fraction

  The (rough) sample target fraction
- seed

  Randomness seed value. Default is a random seed.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sample--note)

sample since 1.4.0

sample\_frac since 1.4.0

![]()

# Returns a stratified sample without replacement

`sampleBy.Rd`

Returns a stratified sample without replacement based on the fraction given on each
stratum.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sampleby--ref-usage)

```text
sampleBy(x, col, fractions, seed)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,character,list,numeric
sampleBy(x, col, fractions, seed)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sampleby--arguments)

- x

  A SparkDataFrame
- col

  column that defines strata
- fractions

  A named list giving sampling fraction for each stratum. If a stratum is
  not specified, we treat its fraction as zero.
- seed

  random seed

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sampleby--value)

A new SparkDataFrame that represents the stratified sample

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sampleby--note)

sampleBy since 1.6.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sampleby--see-also)

Other stat functions:
`[approxQuantile](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-approxquantile)()`,
`[corr](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-corr)()`,
`[cov](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-cov)()`,
`[crosstab](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-crosstab)()`,
`[freqItems](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-freqitems)()`

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sampleby--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
df <- read.json("/path/to/file.json")
sample <- sampleBy(df, "key", fractions, 36)
}
```

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-saveastable--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Save the contents of the SparkDataFrame to a data source as a table

`saveAsTable.Rd`

The data source is specified by the `source` and a set of options (...).
If `source` is not specified, the default data source configured by
spark.sql.sources.default will be used.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-saveastable--ref-usage)

```text
saveAsTable(df, tableName, source = NULL, mode = "error", ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,character
saveAsTable(df, tableName, source = NULL, mode = "error", ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-saveastable--arguments)

- df

  a SparkDataFrame.
- tableName

  a name for the table.
- source

  a name for external data source.
- mode

  one of 'append', 'overwrite', 'error', 'errorifexists', 'ignore'
  save mode (it is 'error' by default)
- ...

  additional option(s) passed to the method.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-saveastable--details)

Additionally, mode is used to specify the behavior of the save operation when
data already exists in the data source. There are four modes:   
'append': Contents of this SparkDataFrame are expected to be appended to existing data.   
'overwrite': Existing data is expected to be overwritten by the contents of this
SparkDataFrame.   
'error' or 'errorifexists': An exception is expected to be thrown.   
'ignore': The save operation is expected to not save the contents of the SparkDataFrame
and to not change the existing data.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-saveastable--note)

saveAsTable since 1.4.0

`select.Rd`

Selects a set of columns with names or Column expressions.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-select--ref-usage)

```sql
select(x, col, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
$(x, name)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
$(x, name) <- value

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,character
select(x, col, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,Column
select(x, col, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,list
select(x, col)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-select--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- col

  a list of columns or single Column or name.
- ...

  additional column(s) if only one column is specified in `col`.
  If more than one column is assigned in `col`, `...`
  should be left empty.
- name

  name of a Column (without being wrapped by `""`).
- value

  a Column or an atomic vector in the length of 1 as literal value, or `NULL`.
  If `NULL`, the specified Column is dropped.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-select--value)

A new SparkDataFrame with selected columns.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-select--note)

$ since 1.4.0

$<- since 1.4.0

select(SparkDataFrame, character) since 1.4.0

select(SparkDataFrame, Column) since 1.4.0

select(SparkDataFrame, list) since 1.4.0

```sql
}
```

![]()

# Set the behavior of job cancellation from jobs started in this thread.

`setInterruptOnCancel.Rd`

Set the behavior of job cancellation from jobs started in this thread.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-setinterruptoncancel--ref-usage)

```text
setInterruptOnCancel(interruptOnCancel)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-setinterruptoncancel--arguments)

- interruptOnCancel

  If true, then job cancellation will result in `Thread.interrupt()`
  being called on the job's executor threads. This is useful to help ensure that the tasks
  are actually stopped in a timely manner, but is off by default due to HDFS-1208, where HDFS
  may respond to Thread.interrupt() by marking nodes as dead.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-setinterruptoncancel--note)

cancelJobGroup since 3.5.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-setinterruptoncancel--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
setInterruptOnCancel(true)
}
```

# Assigns a group ID to all the jobs started by this thread until the group ID is set to a different value or cleared.

Assigns a group ID to all the jobs started by this thread until the group ID is set to a
different value or cleared.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-setjobgroup--ref-usage)

```text

```

  the ID to be assigned to job groups.
- description

- interruptOnCancel

# show

`show.Rd`

If eager evaluation is enabled and the Spark object is a SparkDataFrame, evaluate the
SparkDataFrame and print top rows of the SparkDataFrame, otherwise, print the class
and type information of the Spark object.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-show--ref-usage)

```bash
# S4 method for Column
show(object)

# S4 method for GroupedData
show(object)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
show(object)

# S4 method for WindowSpec
show(object)

# S4 method for StreamingQuery
show(object)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-show--arguments)

- object

  a Spark object. Can be a SparkDataFrame, Column, GroupedData, WindowSpec.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-show--note)

show(Column) since 1.4.0

show(GroupedData) since 1.4.0

show(SparkDataFrame) since 1.4.0

show(WindowSpec) since 2.0.0

show(StreamingQuery) since 2.2.0

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-showdf--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# showDF

`showDF.Rd`

Print the first numRows rows of a SparkDataFrame

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-showdf--ref-usage)

```text
showDF(x, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame
showDF(x, numRows = 20, truncate = TRUE, vertical = FALSE)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-showdf--arguments)

- x

  a SparkDataFrame.
- ...

  further arguments to be passed to or from other methods.
- numRows

  the number of rows to print. Defaults to 20.
- truncate

  whether truncate long strings. If `TRUE`, strings more than
  20 characters will be truncated. However, if set greater than zero,
  truncates strings longer than `truncate` characters and all cells
  will be aligned right.
- vertical

  whether print output rows vertically (one line per column value).

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-showdf--note)

showDF since 1.4.0

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-addfile--css-toggle-btn"></a>

# Add a file or directory to be downloaded with this Spark job on every node.

`spark.addFile.Rd`

The path passed can be either a local file, a file in HDFS (or other Hadoop-supported
filesystems), or an HTTP, HTTPS or FTP URI. To access the file in Spark jobs,
use spark.getSparkFiles(fileName) to find its download location.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-addfile--ref-usage)

```text
spark.addFile(path, recursive = FALSE)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-addfile--arguments)

- path

  The path of the file to be added
- recursive

  Whether to add files recursively from the path. Default is FALSE.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-addfile--details)

A directory can be given if the recursive option is set to true.
Currently directories are only supported for Hadoop-supported filesystems.
Refer Hadoop-supported filesystems at
[https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/HADOOP2/HCFS](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/HADOOP2/HCFS).

Note: A path can be added only once. Subsequent additions of the same path are ignored.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-addfile--note)

spark.addFile since 2.1.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-addfile--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
spark.addFile("~/myfile")
}
```

# Factorization Machines Classification Model — spark.fmClassifier • SparkR

[Skip to contents](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--main)

[
![](https://spark.apache.org/images/spark-logo-rev.svg)](https://spark.apache.org/)
[SparkR](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-index)
4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Factorization Machines Classification Model

`spark.fmClassifier.Rd`

`spark.fmClassifier` fits a factorization classification model against a SparkDataFrame.
Users can call `summary` to print a summary of the fitted model, `predict` to make
predictions on new data, and `write.ml`/`read.ml` to save/load fitted models.
Only categorical data is supported.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--ref-usage)

```text
spark.fmClassifier(data, formula, ...)

# S4 method for SparkDataFrame,formula
spark.fmClassifier(
  data,
  formula,
  factorSize = 8,
  fitLinear = TRUE,
  regParam = 0,
  miniBatchFraction = 1,
  initStd = 0.01,
  maxIter = 100,
  stepSize = 1,
  tol = 1e-06,
  solver = c("adamW", "gd"),
  thresholds = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  handleInvalid = c("error", "keep", "skip")
)

# S4 method for FMClassificationModel
summary(object)

# S4 method for FMClassificationModel
predict(object, newData)

# S4 method for FMClassificationModel,character
write.ml(object, path, overwrite = FALSE)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--arguments)

- data

  a `SparkDataFrame` of observations and labels for model fitting.
- formula

  a symbolic description of the model to be fitted. Currently only a few formula
  operators are supported, including '~', '.', ':', '+', and '-'.
- ...

  additional arguments passed to the method.
- factorSize

  dimensionality of the factors.
- fitLinear

  whether to fit linear term. # TODO Can we express this with formula?
- regParam

  the regularization parameter.
- miniBatchFraction

  the mini-batch fraction parameter.
- initStd

  the standard deviation of initial coefficients.
- maxIter

  maximum iteration number.
- stepSize

  stepSize parameter.
- tol

  convergence tolerance of iterations.
- solver

  solver parameter, supported options: "gd" (minibatch gradient descent) or "adamW".
- thresholds

  in binary classification, in range [0, 1]. If the estimated probability of
  class label 1 is > threshold, then predict 1, else 0. A high threshold
  encourages the model to predict 0 more often; a low threshold encourages the
  model to predict 1 more often. Note: Setting this with threshold p is
  equivalent to setting thresholds c(1-p, p).
- seed

  seed parameter for weights initialization.
- handleInvalid

  How to handle invalid data (unseen labels or NULL values) in features and
  label column of string type.
  Supported options: "skip" (filter out rows with invalid data),
  "error" (throw an error), "keep" (put invalid data in
  a special additional bucket, at index numLabels). Default
  is "error".
- object

  a FM Classification model fitted by `spark.fmClassifier`.
- newData

  a SparkDataFrame for testing.
- path

  The directory where the model is saved.
- overwrite

  Overwrites or not if the output path already exists. Default is FALSE
  which means throw exception if the output path exists.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--value)

`spark.fmClassifier` returns a fitted Factorization Machines Classification Model.
`summary` returns summary information of the fitted model, which is a list.
`predict` returns the predicted values based on a FM Classification model.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--note)

spark.fmClassifier since 3.1.0

summary(FMClassificationModel) since 3.1.0

predict(FMClassificationModel) since 3.1.0

write.ml(FMClassificationModel, character) since 3.1.0

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--see-also)

[read.ml](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-read-ml)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-fmclassifier--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
df <- read.df("data/mllib/sample_binary_classification_data.txt", source = "libsvm")

# fit Factorization Machines Classification Model
model <- spark.fmClassifier(
           df, label ~ features,
           regParam = 0.01, maxIter = 10, fitLinear = TRUE
         )

# get the summary of the model
summary(model)

# make predictions
predictions <- predict(model, df)

# save and load the model
path <- "path/to/model"
write.ml(model, path)
savedModel <- read.ml(path)
summary(savedModel)
}
```

# Run a function over a list of elements, distributing the computations with Spark — spark.lapply • SparkR

[Skip to contents](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--main)

[
![](https://spark.apache.org/images/spark-logo-rev.svg)](https://spark.apache.org/)
[SparkR](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-index)
4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Run a function over a list of elements, distributing the computations with Spark

`spark.lapply.Rd`

Run a function over a list of elements, distributing the computations with Spark. Applies a
function in a manner that is similar to doParallel or lapply to elements of a list.
The computations are distributed using Spark. It is conceptually the same as the following code:
lapply(list, func)

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--ref-usage)

```text
spark.lapply(list, func)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--arguments)

- list

  the list of elements
- func

  a function that takes one argument.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--value)

a list of results (the exact type being determined by the function)

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--details)

Known limitations:

- variable scoping and capture: compared to R's rich support for variable resolutions,
  the distributed nature of SparkR limits how variables are resolved at runtime. All the
  variables that are available through lexical scoping are embedded in the closure of the
  function and available as read-only variables within the function. The environment variables
  should be stored into temporary variables outside the function, and not directly accessed
  within the function.
- loading external packages: In order to use a package, you need to load it inside the
  closure. For example, if you rely on the MASS module, here is how you would use it:

  ```text
      train <- function(hyperparam) {
        library(MASS)
        lm.ridge("y ~ x+z", data, lambda=hyperparam)
        model
      }
    
  ```

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--note)

spark.lapply since 2.0.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-spark-lapply--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
doubled <- spark.lapply(1:10, function(x) {2 * x})
}
```

4.1.1

- [Reference](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-index)
- [Articles](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--)

  [SparkR - Practical Guide](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-articles-sparkr-vignettes)

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Call Java Methods

`sparkR.callJMethod.Rd`

Call a Java method in the JVM running the Spark driver. The return
values are automatically converted to R objects for simple objects. Other
values are returned as "jobj" which are references to objects on JVM.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--ref-usage)

```text
sparkR.callJMethod(x, methodName, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--arguments)

- x

  object to invoke the method on. Should be a "jobj" created by newJObject.
- methodName

  method name to call.
- ...

  parameters to pass to the Java method.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--value)

the return value of the Java method. Either returned as a R object
if it can be deserialized or returned as a "jobj". See details section for more.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--details)

This is a low level function to access the JVM directly and should only be used
for advanced use cases. The arguments and return values that are primitive R
types (like integer, numeric, character, lists) are automatically translated to/from
Java types (like Integer, Double, String, Array). A full list can be found in
serialize.R and deserialize.R in the Apache Spark code base.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--note)

sparkR.callJMethod since 2.0.1

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--see-also)

[sparkR.callJStatic](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic), [sparkR.newJObject](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session() # Need to have a Spark JVM running before calling newJObject
# Create a Java ArrayList and populate it
jarray <- sparkR.newJObject("java.util.ArrayList")
sparkR.callJMethod(jarray, "add", 42L)
sparkR.callJMethod(jarray, "get", 0L) # Will print 42
}
```

# Call Static Java Methods

`sparkR.callJStatic.Rd`

Call a static method in the JVM running the Spark driver. The return
value is automatically converted to R objects for simple objects. Other
values are returned as "jobj" which are references to objects on JVM.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--ref-usage)

```text
sparkR.callJStatic(x, methodName, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--arguments)

- x

  fully qualified Java class name that contains the static method to invoke.
- methodName

  name of static method to invoke.
- ...

  parameters to pass to the Java method.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--value)

the return value of the Java method. Either returned as a R object
if it can be deserialized or returned as a "jobj". See details section for more.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--details)

This is a low level function to access the JVM directly and should only be used
for advanced use cases. The arguments and return values that are primitive R
types (like integer, numeric, character, lists) are automatically translated to/from
Java types (like Integer, Double, String, Array). A full list can be found in
serialize.R and deserialize.R in the Apache Spark code base.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--note)

sparkR.callJStatic since 2.0.1

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--see-also)

[sparkR.callJMethod](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod), [sparkR.newJObject](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session() # Need to have a Spark JVM running before calling callJStatic
sparkR.callJStatic("java.lang.System", "currentTimeMillis")
sparkR.callJStatic("java.lang.System", "getProperty", "java.home")
}
```

# Get Runtime Config from the current active SparkSession

`sparkR.conf.Rd`

Get Runtime Config from the current active SparkSession.
To change SparkSession Runtime Config, please see `[sparkR.session()](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-session)`.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-conf--ref-usage)

```text
sparkR.conf(key, defaultValue)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-conf--arguments)

- key

  (optional) The key of the config to get, if omitted, all config is returned
- defaultValue

  (optional) The default value of the config to return if they config is not
  set, if omitted, the call fails if the config key is not set

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-conf--value)

a list of config values with keys as their names

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-conf--note)

sparkR.conf since 2.0.0

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-conf--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session()
allConfigs <- sparkR.conf()
masterValue <- unlist(sparkR.conf("spark.master"))
namedConfig <- sparkR.conf("spark.executor.memory", "0g")
}
```

# (Deprecated) Initialize a new Spark Context

`sparkR.init-deprecated.Rd`

This function initializes a new SparkContext.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-init-deprecated--ref-usage)

```text
sparkR.init(
  master = "",
  appName = "SparkR",
  sparkHome = Sys.getenv("SPARK_HOME"),
  sparkEnvir = list(),
  sparkExecutorEnv = list(),
  sparkJars = "",
  sparkPackages = ""
)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-init-deprecated--arguments)

- master

  The Spark master URL
- appName

  Application name to register with cluster manager
- sparkHome

  Spark Home directory
- sparkEnvir

  Named list of environment variables to set on worker nodes
- sparkExecutorEnv

  Named list of environment variables to be used when launching executors
- sparkJars

  Character vector of jar files to pass to the worker nodes
- sparkPackages

  Character vector of package coordinates

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-init-deprecated--note)

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-init-deprecated--see-also)

[sparkR.session](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-session)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-init-deprecated--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sc <- sparkR.init("local[2]", "SparkR", "/home/spark")
sc <- sparkR.init("local[2]", "SparkR", "/home/spark",
                 list(spark.executor.memory="1g"))
sc <- sparkR.init("yarn-client", "SparkR", "/home/spark",
                 list(spark.executor.memory="4g"),
                 list(LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/directory of JVM libraries (libjvm.so) on workers/"),
                 c("one.jar", "two.jar", "three.jar"),
                 c("com.databricks:spark-avro_2.11:2.0.1"))
}
```

- <a id="spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--css-toggle-btn"></a>

![]()

# Create Java Objects

`sparkR.newJObject.Rd`

Create a new Java object in the JVM running the Spark driver. The return
value is automatically converted to an R object for simple objects. Other
values are returned as a "jobj" which is a reference to an object on JVM.

## Usage[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--ref-usage)

```text
sparkR.newJObject(x, ...)
```

## Arguments[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--arguments)

- x

  fully qualified Java class name.
- ...

  arguments to be passed to the constructor.

## Value[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--value)

the object created. Either returned as a R object
if it can be deserialized or returned as a "jobj". See details section for more.

## Details[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--details)

This is a low level function to access the JVM directly and should only be used
for advanced use cases. The arguments and return values that are primitive R
types (like integer, numeric, character, lists) are automatically translated to/from
Java types (like Integer, Double, String, Array). A full list can be found in
serialize.R and deserialize.R in the Apache Spark code base.

## Note[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--note)

sparkR.newJObject since 2.0.1

## See also[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--see-also)

[sparkR.callJMethod](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljmethod), [sparkR.callJStatic](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-calljstatic)

## Examples[](#spark-apache-org-docs-latest-api-r-reference-sparkr-newjobject--ref-examples)

```text
if (FALSE) {
sparkR.session() # Need to have a Spark JVM running before calling newJObject
# Create a Java ArrayList and populate it
jarray <- sparkR.newJObject("java.util.ArrayList")
sparkR.callJMethod(jarray, "add", 42L)
sparkR.callJMethod(jarray, "get", 0L) # Will print 42
}
```
